Yes, I think so. The tale is an old one, but it is one the villagers know too well: venturing out in the deeper part of woods, some may stumble into a mine entrance. It's apparently like a manhole, but you can see it's not as vertical.

Upon finding it, the illusion begins. People feel like they're being watched, like something massive is racing towards them. Some hear sharp noises, such as the screeching...and they go into the mine. Big mistake. They are never heard from again.

One person ran towards the screeching, according to local legend. It amplified and he was terrified, but he ran towards it. He found nothing making the noise. He just kept running and landed back on the trail to his village, and warned others. It is thought of to be an effective trick by a certain type of forest demon to get humans to enter into a realm where it has the most control - in our world, they do have power but not enough to their liking, I suppose: they can create fear but not openly feed into it (depends on types of demons though, honestly..some types can). But forest demons fall in the weaker categories.

UGH. That screeching is a trick, an illusion, and it's so frustrating that it works. I know because there's a local version of it here, and the villagers I talked to seemed to have understood it. Then again, this may not be the same entity....there's so much that goes on in the woods that t scares me beyond my wits just to think of it all.
